conventions.evidence: Ships a Pest test alongside the code (tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:89-183); docs kept in sync (.env.example, docs/ops/devops.md, docs/ops/logging.md) and CHANGELOG.md:12 entry under [Unreleased] > Added; class PHPDoc updated (DiscordOpsAlert.php:19-22); private const naming SnowflakePattern matches sibling BearerLikePattern. No Livewire/Actions/migration concerns apply.

security.evidence: Strict allowlist validation of the mention id: anchored regex '/^[0-9]{17,20}$/' (DiscordOpsAlert.php:32) applied after trim (line 102), so @everyone/@here, letters, negatives and embedded newline/'>' injections are rejected; trim removes any trailing newline that '$' would otherwise tolerate. Non-scalar config types return null (line 98). Existing redaction and URL-free failure logging are unchanged.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:89-116 valid ids (string, int, surrounding whitespace, 20 digits) asserting the mention is the last line; :118-132 null/''/whitespace emit no '<@'; :134-159 invalid values incl. '@everyone', '@here', 'abc', '123', 21 digits, "123\n@everyone", "123> \n@everyone", trailing letter, negative, bool; :161-183 truncation keeps the mention with total length exactly 1800. The existing no-mention 1800-char test (line 86) still covers unchanged behavior. Only gap: no explicit test that a configured mention with an empty webhook URL is still a no-op.

simplicity.evidence: Minimal change: one regex constant, one small private mention() helper and a 7-line branch in formatContent() (DiscordOpsAlert.php:75-84); reuses the existing MaxContentLength constant and mb_* functions; no new classes or abstractions.

readability.evidence: Clear names (mention(), SnowflakePattern, $bodyLimit) and a short PHPDoc on mention() (DiscordOpsAlert.php:90-92). Minor awkwardness in the test: explode("\n", $content)[count(explode("\n", $content)) - 1] (DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:106) computes the split twice instead of using last()/array_pop; test setup is repeated per test, matching the existing file's style.

scope.evidence: All edits serve the task: config key, env example, class change, docs required by requirement 6, CHANGELOG entry required by project conventions, and tests. No unrelated refactors; the devops.md Config line edit only adds DISCORD_MENTION_ID.

issues.explanation: No test asserts that send() stays a no-op (Http::assertNothingSent) when a valid mention id is configured but the webhook URL is empty, though the code path is unchanged.

The last-line check calls explode twice inline; Str::afterLast or last(explode(...)) would read more clearly, and it is largely redundant with the toEndWith assertion plus a check for the preceding newline.

review.summary: The change adds an optional DISCORD_MENTION_ID config, validates it strictly as a 17-20 digit snowflake (trimmed, int accepted), and appends <@ID> on its own line while reserving room for it within the 1800-character cap. Tests cover valid, empty, invalid/injection and truncation cases, and the env example, ops docs and CHANGELOG are updated. Only trivial test nits remain, so I would approve it.
